- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show upward bias after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70s to 75s), often overshooting by 2–5%.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion after peaks; prices tend to drop faster than forecasted.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the 30d window.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, leading to premature stabilization.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to account for sudden drops or sharp reversals near the end of the window.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias — starts from recent high prices and doesn’t adjust for new data or policy shocks.
- Overconfidence in linear trends; ignores non-linear corrections or policy-induced price corrections.
